group.label: Memoirs · The Making of the Goddess Documentary

lines.text: I started by visiting a refugee shelter. There was a little girl smiling despite the bandages wrapped around her head, saying the Goddesses had saved her. An elderly man in a wheelchair sang the Goddesses' praises, saying they'd carried him here. A young couple held each other tightly, saying they'd found their child thanks to the Goddesses. They had all come from different places, but the name they spoke of was the same.
Wasn't their role just to fight and defeat the Raptures?

A mass-produced Nikke I met behind the front lines told me that seeing the Goddess Squad had given her the courage to return to the battlefield. Whenever she felt like she was about to break, she said she thought of them and found the strength to get back up.
It was the same even in places the media didn't cover. No matter where I went or whom I met, the Goddesses were more than just a symbol. They were a source of hope for the people.
At the very least, they weren't the heroes I initially thought they were, all glitter and no substance. But I still haven't met them myself. I have to meet them in person, no matter what it takes.
